patch.value: The current 18-repository fleet is release-healthy and every published package passed isolated install, activation, doctor blocking checks, and runtime contract exposure. However, none of the 18 repositories declares a lint script or coverage gate; hand-authored TypeScript uses many explicit any annotations; a cross-repository duplicate scan found 42 clone groups and 2,284 duplicated lines, led by 17 copies of the merge-driver preparation script and a vendored pm-graph implementation inside pm-web; several extensions still emit global renderer/service override warnings; package dependency placement and floors vary; and isolated install time has large outliers. The host already owns reusable smoke and SDK authoring primitives. This feature defines one shared preset/workflow and evidence schema so Community, Verified, and Featured labels reflect reproducible package quality rather than repository-local convention. It must compose with pm-quzx rather than duplicate its beads/todos and dependency-range decisions.
Official ecosystem conformance gate: shared quality, security, SDK-boundary, duplication, and install-performance policy

Turn the ecosystem trust ladder into one reusable, machine-readable conformance gate for every official external pm package and future Verified package, covering source quality through published-artifact runtime proof.

A machine-readable matrix inventories every official external package and future candidate; a reusable package-owned preset or workflow enforces typecheck, lint, complexity, dead-export analysis, tests, coverage, duplication ratchet, production dependency audit, pack verification, isolated install/activate/doctor, and runtime action-contract smoke; shared maintenance logic is versioned once instead of copied across repositories; intentional shared code is documented and large vendored implementations such as pm-graph inside pm-web are replaced by an explicit package/build dependency or separately justified boundary; public SDK imports only use supported exports and subprocess fallback is limited to explicit process boundaries; package service/renderer ownership produces zero unexplained doctor warnings; install latency is measured with a documented budget and retry/noise policy; published npm artifacts and exact default-branch heads are both proven; no quality threshold is weakened and no package feature is removed.

value.author: claude-code-agent
value.text: Duplicate-check evidence: all-status search found pm-vnjh for the shipped external smoke harness, pm-o8um for the open trust ladder, pm-quzx for dependency ranges and duplicate beads/todos homes, pm-92if for core-repo quality, and pm-usfg for the public SDK boundary. None owns a fleet-wide lint, coverage, duplication, dead-code, security, and install-latency conformance floor, so this focused child extends pm-o8um and relates to those canonical owners.

value.text: Passing isolated install and runtime smoke proves package reachability, not source maintainability. Verified ecosystem trust needs a second layer that evaluates lint, coverage, duplication, dead exports, dependency policy, published artifacts, service ownership, and install cost across repository boundaries.
